Our ops team attached a short set of traces and dashboards — the degradation seems correlated with a spike of long-running requests from a batch job we started at 02:00 PT. We urgently need a plan to stabilize and an ETA for resolution.

Attachments: elmbridge_latency_traces.zip, monitoring_screenshots.png

Adding technical context from ops triage (notes from call):

Summary of initial findings:
- Observed sustained request queues on Elmbridge's dedicated pool; queue length climbed ~x8 in <15m.
- Concurrency cap for that pool hit the configured limit (client-specific cap). New requests were buffered rather than routed to other healthy workers.
- Evidence of KV cache contamination where a long-running batch filled shared CPU resources causing additional head-of-line blocking.
- A subset of routed requests fell back to a quantized model variant with slower I/O paths, amplifying tail.

Immediate mitigations executed (08:40–08:55):
- Temporarily raised concurrency cap on Elmbridge's Dedicated pool by +40% (mitigation for 30 mins while we assess).
- Enabled emergency prefix K/V cache invalidation for the suspected job namespace (reduced avg token time on tests).
- De-prioritized non-interactive batch traffic by applying traffic-class routing; interactive routes preserved.

Next steps (owners):
- David (eng): collect pprof traces and a short heap/CPU timeline from the affected nodes — attaching artifacts to the Drive link.
- Marissa (SRE): validate no persistent queue transfer happened to other tenants and confirm isolation.
- Kimberly / Karthik: coordinate the customer communication and procurement threads.

Attachments referenced: elmbridge_latency_traces.zip (ingested), pprof_samples_elmbridge.tgz (uploaded to drive)

I'll follow up with a 2-hour readout.

David Kim
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Sara — quick update and what to expect in the next hours: 

What we did (already applied):
- Raised Elmbridge pool concurrency cap +40% (30-minute window) — immediate drop in enqueued requests observed.
- Emergency cache invalidation for the job namespace — reduced token processing time in tests by ~35%.
- Applied traffic-class routing to throttle the identified batch job traffic.

Expected timeline:
- 30–45 min: measurable restoration of P95/P99 for interactive flows.
- 2 hours: engineering readout with root-cause notes and permanent mitigation plan.
- 4 hours: exec summary and proposed SLA remediation (if required).

Ask of Elmbridge:
- Please pause/scale down the batch job for 20–30 minutes if possible (this is the fastest way to get to green).
- If pause is not feasible, please share the job's source IP and approximate concurrency so we can pin and route it.

Executive handoff: Karthik will lead the commercial outreach, and I'll prepare a one-page exec note for your CTO and our VP of Customer Success. If you'd like a joint call with our Head of Reliability, we can set that up in the 2–4 hour window.

Attached: SLA_exception_request.docx (pre-populated form for credits/SLA exemptions)

Thanks for staying patient — we'll keep this thread as the primary comms channel.
